The real issue isn't partisan theatrics—it's systemic rot. The Senate's Medicaid cuts expose a rigged system where pharmaceutical giants pocket billions through inflated drug prices while bureaucrats protect consultant kickbacks. Both parties enabled this mess by letting hospital networks exploit provider taxes and state-directed payment schemes.

True reform means auditing every dollar, ending cost-plus contracting, and dismantling the middlemen profiting from suffering.

Until Congress stops protecting Big Pharma's monopoly power and Medicaid's billing fraud, no bill—big or beautiful—will fix healthcare's core corruption.

The dialysis industry’s profit-first model is a glaring example of systemic failure, where corporate greed eclipses patient safety. With DaVita and Fresenius controlling 80% of clinics, their focus on shareholder returns—not care—fuels deadly shortcuts: rushed treatments, understaffed facilities, and retaliatory discharges. Federal data shows over 5,000 patients were kicked off dialysis in a decade, nearly 1,000 dying within a year—disproportionately Black Americans, who face 53% of terminations despite being 33% of the patient population.

CMS’s enforcement is a joke, letting clinics weaponize “noncompliance” to dump costly patients while rubber-stamping fabricated claims. This isn’t about “difficult” patients; it’s about a broken system where ER networks enable clinics to prioritize profit margins over lives.

The Trump administration’s push for healthcare efficiency must crack down on these predatory practices, ensuring clinics serve people—not portfolios—by mandating transparency, enforcing discharge protocols, and holding corporations accountable for prioritizing profits over survival.
